Reasoning: that card shipped first per its own header comment's explicit rule; its shape is already merged, deployed (0% canary), and staging-probed against production; PR #75 was not yet merged and had exactly one disposable test row. LESSON: Two cards racing to define the same shared contract can both pass CI and both be individually correct while disagreeing with each other -- CI green is necessary but not sufficient evidence a store-shape PR is safe to merge when another card claims to define the same store.

When a prior claimant's PR already ran a live end-to-end test against production, check schema_migrations and the actual live table before assuming a migration file describes reality -- it may already be applied, meaning the fix is a new migration, not an edit to the old one.

The Factory's gate-rail-cli.mjs is intentionally narrow (one county, one rail, 20s statement_timeout) specifically so it survives store contention that defeats ad hoc broad SELECTs -- when a raw query times out under concurrent writer load, reach for the purpose-built narrow instrument instead of retrying the broad one with a longer timeout.
